# REAL: radio -> network, one message, Motorola TMS framing on port 4007 — what a
# 6X2 Pro emits when its channel SMS format is M-SMS. The sibling fixture
# capture-radio-etsi.txt is the same radio with the format set to DMR Standard.
#
# Addressed to 9000001, a node-local bot-range ID that exists nowhere. The
# transfer crosses the loopback anyway, which is the premise the bot framework's
# intercept rests on: nothing has to answer for the frames to be observable.
#
# UNCONFIRMED data (DPF 0x02), and that is the point of the fixture as much as the
# text is. parseDataHeader declines DPFConfirmedData outright, so a clean decode is
# itself the evidence — it settles D-F9 and keeps the inbound codec small.
#
# Captured off the bench modem loopback 2026-08-17, MMDVM-Host -> DMRGateway leg
# only (the relay is in the path on that node, so every burst is on the wire twice
# and the other leg would duplicate every line here). One burst per line:
# <data-type from the DMRD flags byte> <33 bytes hex>.
#
# Five preamble CSBKs (03), one data header (06), six rate-1/2 blocks (07).
# Decodes to "TFRT WAYPOINT". Note five preambles, not the nine this package sends
# by default — the radio is more frugal than DefaultPreambles assumes.
#
# Bench: Pi 3 + MMDVM_HS_Dual_Hat, KN4OQW / 3180202, colour code 2, timeslot 2
# (Slot1=0 on that node). Radio: BTECH DMR-6X2 Pro, SMS Format M-SMS.
#
# Sanitization: 3180202 is the maintainer's own public RadioID and 9000001 is
# node-local and belongs to nobody, so neither is third-party PII. Rewriting either
# would invalidate every checksum in the file.
